text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] spike in 5xx from EU cluster euc1 (AZ-b) observed on ALB -> NLB -> Envoy path. Paging oncall @Mia. Potential customer impact: API error rate increased for EU customers.

Mia: I'm on the page. Kicking off triage: checking ALB/NLB target health and ingress pods. Raj, can you pull NLB target metrics and target health?

Raj: grabbing target health now. Quick notes: an abnormal number of connections resetting for targets in euc1-b; NLB metrics show surge in TCP_Reset_Count and TargetHealth shows many unhealthy.

Sam: checklist for anyone joining — 1) which load balancer hop is failing (ALB vs NLB), 2) check kube nodes in AZ-b for kernel conntrack logs, 3) inspect envoy upstream error rates and restart counts. If it's isolated to AZ-b we can shift traffic while we remediate.

Mia: flow is ALB fronting NLB which fans to k8s nodes running Envoy. Errors appear concentrated on NLB->targets in euc1-b. Running scrips now.

Raj: commands I'm running:```
# inspect target health
aws elbv2 describe-target-health --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:eu-central-1:123456789012:targetgroup/tg-ingress-euc1b/abcd1234
# NLB metrics
aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace AWS/NetworkELB --metric-name TCP_Reset_Count --dimensions Name=LoadBalancer,Value=app/my-nlb/xyz --start-time 2026-03-15T00:00:00Z --end-time 2026-03-15T01:00:00Z --period 60 --statistics Sum
```

Mia: Envoy logs from the ingress namespace showing many "connection reset by peer" and upstream 502/503. Pod list:```
kubectl -n ingress get pods -o wide
NAME                                  READY   STATUS    RESTARTS
ingress-envoy-7f9d-aaa               2/2     Running   1
ingress-envoy-7f9d-bbb               2/2     Running   15
ingress-controller-1                 1/1     Running   0
```

Sam: bbb has elevated restarts, likely hitting connection limits. Also check dmesg on nodes for nf_conntrack warnings — that matches reset patterns.

Lisa: on the nodes in euc1-b I see kernel messages: "nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet" on two worker nodes. Conntrack exhaustion would produce exactly these resets.

Mia: immediate mitigations ideas: A) increase net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max on affected nodes, B) restart/replace pods on those nodes, C) scale up ingress replicas, D) temporarily shift traffic off AZ-b via Route53 weighted policy. Which to run first?

Raj: applying conntrack bump via SSM to the two affected instances now. Command:```
sudo sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1500000
echo 'net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=1500000' >> /etc/sysctl.conf
```

Raj: also reducing conntrack timeouts to lower churn. Pushing both changes.

Mia: scaling ingress deployment to six replicas to add capacity:```
kubectl -n ingress scale deploy ingress-envoy --replicas=6
```

Sam: recommend draining the worst-restarted pod so it reschedules onto a node with expanded conntrack table. I'll cordon+drain one node after confirming capacity.

Mia: deleting pod ingress-envoy-7f9d-bbb to force a restart elsewhere:```
kubectl -n ingress delete pod ingress-envoy-7f9d-bbb
```

devops-bot: rollout restart triggered by @Mia: rollout restart deployment/ingress-envoy -n ingress.

Mia: after conntrack increases + pod rotation + scaling, 5xx rate reduced from ~45% to ~9% in ~7 minutes. Partial mitigation achieved.

Lisa: residual resets remain but far fewer. Suggest we change healthcheck type to TCP and lower deregistration delay on the NLB target group to allow faster failover during recovery.

Raj: updating target-group attributes now:```
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn <arn> --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn <arn> --attributes Key=stickiness.enabled,Value=false
```

Sam: going to apply a temporary Route53 weight change to move traffic off euc1-b (0% weight) to euc1-a/c. Executing controlled change.

Mia: Route53 change submitted, propagation in progress:```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z999 --change-batch file://failover-euc1b-zero-weight.json
```

Mia: after weighted failover, user-visible errors returned to baseline (<1%) within a few minutes. Note: customers using long-lived TCP connections may have experienced disconnects during the shift.

support-bot: creating CS ticket for impacted customers and flagging accounts with >5% error rates in last 30m. Ticket created: CS-9876.

Sam: I'll own the incident postmortem and the follow-ups: enforce higher conntrack defaults across euc1, revisit kube-proxy conntrack settings, add ASG scale targets for ingress nodes, and add node-level nf_conntrack alerts. Handoff to me at 20:35 UTC.

Mia: handing off. Summary for notes: root cause = conntrack table exhaustion on nodes in euc1-b causing NLB TCP resets -> Envoy upstream errors -> ALB 5xx spike. Mitigations = increased nf_conntrack_max, restarted ingress pods, scaled replicas, adjusted NLB healthchecks, temporary Route53 traffic shift. Customer impact = ~22 minutes of elevated 5xx in EU, no data loss.

Sam: I'll file the incident doc and schedule a follow-up RCA meeting. Thanks @Mia, @Raj, @Lisa and bots for quick work.

Mia: closing active page; if anything re-surges ping @Sam directly. :thumbsup:
